Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1775
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1775
- **Title**: gh-1759 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1759` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +211
- **Deletions**: -80
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:57:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T23:47:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1759
### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. Resume itself worked (`Resuming transfer from byte position …` in the logs), but the pre-loop `rm -f "$ZIP"` discarded each run's partial, so no daily run ever banked durable progress. The cache fallback was cold too: the `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` entry saved 10-20 06:02Z was LRU-evicted by the repo's daily cache churn before 10-21 19:03Z (both jobs logged `Cache not found`).

### Previous Attempt
gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.
- ci.yml / nightly.yml WasmRun steps run on GitHub-hosted runners (600s attempts, datacenter links) — intentionally unchanged.

Potential issues I've identified so far:

1. **Pre-loop digest gate vs. incomplete partial**: If the persisted partial is INCOMPLETE (e.g., 30MB of 97MB), the pre-loop gate's shasum fails (of course) → enters loop → curl -C - resumes from 30MB. Good — the gate only skips on complete+valid.

2. **`wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null`** — if $ZIP doesn't exist (all attempts failed before creating the file), bash prints an error to stderr (the redirect error isn't suppressed because `< "$ZIP"` is processed before `2>/dev/null`), but the `|| echo 0` handles the pipeline failure. Cosmetic log noise; behavior correct (got=0 → incomplete branch → keep → exit 1). Very minor.

Wait, actually — one more check: does curl with `--fail` on a 404 create the output file? Modern curl: `-o` file is created/opened when the transfer starts... Actually with `--fail`, since curl 7.76? No — let me think. There's a curl behavior: "--fail ... fail silently (no output at all) on server errors" and importantly, since curl 7.75.0? Hmm, there was a change: "curl --fail no longer writes the error body". And regarding file creation: curl creates the output file lazily on first write? No — curl creates/truncates the output file BEFORE sending the request, historically. Actually, I recall `curl -o out http://404` leaves a 0-byte out file. Yes, curl creates the output file early. So a 404 with --fail typically leaves a 0-byte $ZIP. Either way (file exists 0 bytes, or doesn't exist), got=0 → keep branch → exit 1. Correct.

3. **The success check `if [ "$got" -eq "$ASET_BYTES" ] && echo ... | shasum -a 256 -c -; then`** — note shasum here does NOT suppress stderr/stdout — on success it prints "$ZIP: OK" to stdout. Good for logs.

4. **`[ "$got" -lt "$ASET_BYTES" ]` keep branch when $ZIP missing entirely** — got=0 → keep → exit 1 with message "resumes from byte 0". Fine.

5. **Oversize partial (got > ASET_BYTES) with VALID digest impossible** — fine.

6. **The one hole: complete-size partial (got == ASET_BYTES) with WRONG digest → purge branch.** But note: the pre-loop gate would ALSO have failed for this zip, so the loop runs, 4 × 416-failures (fast), then purge. OK.

7. **NOW — the interesting one: what if `curl` succeeds on attempt N (break) but the file is INCOMPLETE?** As analyzed, curl exit 0 with -C - means the full remaining range was received. But consider: GitHub redirects `-L` to S3/objects.githubusercontent.com — if the redirect target serves the FULL file ignoring the Range header... with `-C -`, curl first makes a HEAD-ish? No: with `-C -`, curl asks the server for the range; the server (S3) honors Range. If a server ignores Range and returns 200 full-content while resuming, curl errors with 33 ("HTTP server doesn't seem to support byte ranges"). Hmm, is that exactly right? curl with `-C -` receiving a 200 instead of 206: it aborts with error 33. Yes.

  BUT the subtle one: what if the response is 206 but with a SHORT body and clean TLS close → curl exit 18 (partial file) → treated as failure → retry. Fine.

8. **`set -e` interaction with `if curl ...; then break; fi`** — curl failure inside if-condition is fine.

9. **The `attempt` variable after loop when the loop is skipped**: If the pre-loop gate succeeds (skip download), the `for` loop never runs, `unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"` runs — $ZIP is the complete valid zip. Good.

10. **`unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"` — unzip into shared DEST while the OTHER arch job might be doing the same** — pre-existing shared-DEST race, content identical. Not new. I might mention as a general observation, pre-existing.

11. **The 20-min timeout vs. the workflow's job-level timeout** — need to check if job-level timeout-minutes exists that's < 20. Let me check.

12. **`ASET_BYTES`/`ASET_DIGEST` hardcoded per asset URL** — if the URL is ever bumped, the digest must be updated; the test pins the digest value so drift is caught. Good.

13. **Comment math**: "Worst case with the gh-1759 budget: 4 × 240s max-time + 3 × 5s sleeps = 975s, + connect + unzip + slack ≈ 1035s < the 20-min (120s) cap." — connect-timeout is inside --max-time, so 4 × 240 already covers connect. The +60s reserve covers shasum (twice: pre-loop gate + post-loop check — each ~97MB hash) + wc + unzip + ls. shasum -a 256 on a 97MB file: Digest::SHA via Perl is roughly 100-250MB/s on Apple Silicon → <1s each. unzip -q of a 92.7MB zip → few seconds. OK, reserve is adequate.

14. **`timeout-minutes: 20` — but is there a job-level timeout?** Let me check the workflow for `timeout-minutes:` at job level. Also check `runs-on` for build-macos — self-hosted runners: GitHub's default job timeout is 360 minutes; step timeouts work on self-hosted.

15. **The `if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]`** — hardcodes 4; consistent with `for attempt in 1 2 3 4`. If someone bumps to 5 in one place only, the last-atempt message misfires (prints "resuming in 5s..." then loop ends). Minor maintainability nit; the test's DownloadLoop.parse counts attempts and the worst-case check would catch budget drift but not this desync.   # Issue #280 AC3: nightly RELEASE-mode build matrix. The PR legs in
  # ci.yml build --debug (compile-truth); release-only concerns —
  # tree-shaking, R8/minify, dart2js optimisation, icon stripping — are
  # verified here, plus linux/windows bonus targets (the app does not ship
  # there officially yet, so they stay nightly-only per the card's
  # non-goals). A red leg feeds the deduped nightly-red issue via the
  # auto-issue job below.
  build-release:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} (release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build macos --release
          - target: ios
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build ios --release --no-codesign
          - target: android
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build apk --flavor store --release
          - target: web
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build web --release
      # The prebuilt WasmRun XCFramework is excluded from git; Apple builds
      # fail in the Podfile FFI-symbol check without it. Pinned upstream
      # release, same fallback as the ci.yml build legs.
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun framework (Apple targets)
        if: matrix.target == 'ios' || matrix.target == 'macos'
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/${{ matrix.target }}/Frameworks"
          rm -rf "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
            -o /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip \
            https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip
          unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      # The macOS Podfile bundles the LiteRT-LM companion dylibs via a
      # Runner script phase that fails on a fresh runner ("Could not find
      # macOS companion dylibs") — seed from the pinned upstream native
      # release, sha256-verified (same incantation as build-macos.yml).
      - name: Ensure flutter_gemma macOS companion dylibs
        if: matrix.target == 'macos'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GEMMA_CACHE="$HOME/Library/Caches/flutter_gemma/native/macos_arm64"

404:         timeout-minutes: 20
405:         run: |
406:           set -euo pipefail
407:           # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
408:           # 1) actions/cache hit (keyed by the release tag) — warm until the
409:           #    repo's daily cache churn LRU-evicts the entry (saved 10-20
410:           #    06:02Z, gone by 10-21 19:03Z: gh-1759 ran cold twice);
411:           # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
412:           # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the step
413:           #    cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): retries live in THIS
414:           #    bash loop, not curl --retry (which adds N MORE attempts AND
415:           #    restarts+truncates instead of resuming). Worst case with the
416:           #    gh-1759 budget: 4 × 240s max-time + 3 × 5s sleeps = 975s,
417:           #    + connect + unzip + slack ≈ 1035s < the 20-min (1200s) cap.
418:           #
419:           #    gh-1759: the gh-1149 budget (3 × 240s) was sized for this
420:           #    link's good-day ~300KB/s. The 10-21 daily run measured
421:           #    40–108KB/s (cold cache, both arch jobs): 3 × 240s banked
422:           #    only 29.5MB (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) of the 97,238,501-byte
423:           #    asset and the leg went red. Resume worked (`Resuming
424:           #    transfer from byte position …` in the logs) — the wire
425:           #    budget was simply too small, and the old pre-loop wipe
426:           #    threw each run's partial away, so a slow-link day never
427:           #    banked durable progress and the leg could not self-heal.
428:           #    Fixes: (a) the per-arch /tmp partial now PERSISTS across
429:           #    runs — -C - resumes it within the step AND across daily
430:           #    runs (macOS prunes only 3-day-untouched /tmp files; a daily
431:           #    run touches it) until the asset completes and the
432:           #    actions/cache post-step saves the framework; (b) the loop
433:           #    grew to 4 × 240s under a 20-min step cap.
434:           LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
435:           DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
436:           # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
437:           # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
438:           # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
439:           # let one job's cleanup unlink the other's in-flight partial,
440:           # then both curls interleave bytes into one path.
441:           ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
442:           # The release asset is immutable per tag — pin its digest so a
443:           # wrong-content-but-valid-zip cannot slip past unzip CRC32 into
444:           # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache (same pattern
445:           # as the litertlm download above). The pinned byte size tells a
446:           # truncated download (KEEP the partial — the next run resumes
447:           # it) apart from a complete-but-wrong one (PURGE and restart).
448:           ASSET_DIGEST="aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98"
449:           ASSET_BYTES=97238501
450:           mkdir -p "$DEST"
451:           if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
452:             echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
453:           elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
454:             echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
455:             cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
456:           else
457:             echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
458:             # The partial is deliberately NOT deleted between runs
459:             # (gh-1759): it is exactly what -C - is for. If the persisted
460:             # zip is already complete AND digest-valid, skip the download
461:             # — a -C - attempt against a complete file gets HTTP 416 and
462:             # reads success as failure.
463:             if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
464:               echo "Complete, digest-valid $ZIP persisted from an earlier run — skipping download"
465:             else
466:               for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
467:                 # --fail: without it curl exits 0 on HTTP 404/5xx and writes
468:                 # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error
469:                 # engages this loop's retries. -C - makes each attempt
470:                 # RESUME the partial zip (Range requests), so slow links
471:                 # make forward progress within this step AND across runs.
472:                 if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
473:                   -o "$ZIP" \
474:                   https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
475:                   break
476:                 fi
477:                 if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]; then
478:                   echo "download attempt $attempt failed — out of loop attempts" >&2
479:                 else
480:                   echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
481:                   sleep 5
482:                 fi
483:               done
484:               got=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || echo 0)
485:               if [ "$got" -eq "$ASSET_BYTES" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -; then
486:                 : # complete and authentic — fall through to unzip
487:               elif [ "$got" -lt "$ASSET_BYTES" ]; then
488:                 echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip incomplete: $got / $ASSET_BYTES bytes after $attempt attempts — keeping the partial; the next run resumes from byte $got (gh-1759)" >&2

493:                 exit 1
494:               fi

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. - **PR #**: 1775
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1775
- **Title**: gh-1759 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1759` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +211
- **Deletions**: -80
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:57:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T23:47:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1759
### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. Resume itself worked (`Resuming transfer from byte position …` in the logs), but the pre-loop `rm -f "$ZIP"` discarded each run's partial, so no daily run ever banked durable progress. The cache fallback was cold too: the `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` entry saved 10-20 06:02Z was LRU-evicted by the repo's daily cache churn before 10-21 19:03Z (both jobs logged `Cache not found`).

### Previous Attempt
gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.
- ci.yml / nightly.yml WasmRun steps run on GitHub-hosted runners (600s attempts, datacenter links) — intentionally unchanged.

Confirmed: against the OLD workflow, 2 of 5 tests fail (RED as claimed); against the NEW workflow, 5 of 5 pass (GREEN as claimed). The PR description's claims are verified.

Now let me do a careful logic analysis of the shell changes. Let me re-examine the new restore step script for correctness issues:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
...
ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${ matrix.arch }}.zip"
ASET_DIGEST="aca903d73202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98"
ASET_BYTES=97238501
mkdir -p "$DEST"
if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
 echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
 echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
 cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
else
 echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
 if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$ASET_DIGEST $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   echo "Complete, digest-valid $ZIP persisted from an earlier run — skipping download"
 else
   for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
     if curl --fail -L -C --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
       -o "$ZIP" \
       https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
       break
     fi
     if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]; then
       echo "download attempt $attempt failed — out of loop attempts" >&2
     else
       echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
       sleep 5
     fi
   done
   got=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' || echo 0)
   if [ "$got" -eq "$ASET_BYTES" ] && echo "$ASET_DIGEST $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -; then
     : # complete and authentic — fall through to unzip
   elif [ "$got" -lt "$ASET_BYTES" ]; then
     echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip incomplete: $got / $ASET_BYTES bytes after $attempt attempts — keeping the partial; the next run resumes from byte $got (gh-1759)" >&2
     exit 1
   else
     echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip is $got bytes (expected $ASET_BYTES) or failed its pinned sha256 — purging it so the next run restarts clean" >&2
     rm -f "$ZIP"
     exit 1
   fi
 fi
 unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
fi
ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
``

Potential issues I've identified so far:

1. **Pre-loop digest gate vs. incomplete partial**: If the persisted partial is INCOMPLETE (e.g., 30MB of 97MB), the pre-loop gate's shasum fails (of course) → enters loop → curl -C - resumes from 30MB. Good — the gate only skips on complete+valid.

2. **`wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null`** — if $ZIP doesn't exist (all attempts failed before creating the file), bash prints an error to stderr (the redirect error isn't suppressed because `< "$ZIP"` is processed before `2>/dev/null`), but the `|| echo 0` handles the pipeline failure. Cosmetic log noise; behavior correct (got=0 → incomplete branch → keep → exit 1). Very minor.

Wait, actually — one more check: does curl with `--fail` on a 404 create the output file? Modern curl: `-o` file is created/opened when the transfer starts... Actually with `--fail`, since curl 7.76? No — let me think. There's a curl behavior: "--fail ... fail silently (no output at all) on server errors" and importantly, since curl 7.75.0? Hmm, there was a change: "curl --fail no longer writes the error body". And regarding file creation: curl creates the output file lazily on first write? No — curl creates/truncates the output file BEFORE sending the request, historically. Actually, I recall `curl -o out http://404` leaves a 0-byte out file. Yes, curl creates the output file early. So a 404 with --fail typically leaves a 0-byte $ZIP. Either way (file exists 0 bytes, or doesn't exist), got=0 → keep branch → exit 1. Correct.

3. **The success check `if [ "$got" -eq "$ASET_BYTES" ] && echo ... | shasum -a 256 -c -; then`** — note shasum here does NOT suppress stderr/stdout — on success it prints "$ZIP: OK" to stdout. Good for logs.

4. **`[ "$got" -lt "$ASET_BYTES" ]` keep branch when $ZIP missing entirely** — got=0 → keep → exit 1 with message "resumes from byte 0". Fine.

5. **Oversize partial (got > ASET_BYTES) with VALID digest impossible** — fine.

6. **The one hole: complete-size partial (got == ASET_BYTES) with WRONG digest → purge branch.** But note: the pre-loop gate would ALSO have failed for this zip, so the loop runs, 4 × 416-failures (fast), then purge. OK.

7. **NOW — the interesting one: what if `curl` succeeds on attempt N (break) but the file is INCOMPLETE?** As analyzed, curl exit 0 with -C - means the full remaining range was received. But consider: GitHub redirects `-L` to S3/objects.githubusercontent.com — if the redirect target serves the FULL file ignoring the Range header... with `-C -`, curl first makes a HEAD-ish? No: with `-C -`, curl asks the server for the range; the server (S3) honors Range. If a server ignores Range and returns 200 full-content while resuming, curl errors with 33 ("HTTP server doesn't seem to support byte ranges"). Hmm, is that exactly right? curl with `-C -` receiving a 200 instead of 206: it aborts with error 33. Yes.

  BUT the subtle one: what if the response is 206 but with a SHORT body and clean TLS close → curl exit 18 (partial file) → treated as failure → retry. Fine.

8. **`set -e` interaction with `if curl ...; then break; fi`** — curl failure inside if-condition is fine.

9. **The `attempt` variable after loop when the loop is skipped**: If the pre-loop gate succeeds (skip download), the `for` loop never runs, `unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"` runs — $ZIP is the complete valid zip. Good.

10. **`unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"` — unzip into shared DEST while the OTHER arch job might be doing the same** — pre-existing shared-DEST race, content identical. Not new. I might mention as a general observation, pre-existing.

11. **The 20-min timeout vs. the workflow's job-level timeout** — need to check if job-level timeout-minutes exists that's < 20. Let me check.

12. **`ASET_BYTES`/`ASET_DIGEST` hardcoded per asset URL** — if the URL is ever bumped, the digest must be updated; the test pins the digest value so drift is caught. Good.

13. **Comment math**: "Worst case with the gh-1759 budget: 4 × 240s max-time + 3 × 5s sleeps = 975s, + connect + unzip + slack ≈ 1035s < the 20-min (120s) cap." — connect-timeout is inside --max-time, so 4 × 240 already covers connect. The +60s reserve covers shasum (twice: pre-loop gate + post-loop check — each ~97MB hash) + wc + unzip + ls. shasum -a 256 on a 97MB file: Digest::SHA via Perl is roughly 100-250MB/s on Apple Silicon → <1s each. unzip -q of a 92.7MB zip → few seconds. OK, reserve is adequate.

14. **`timeout-minutes: 20` — but is there a job-level timeout?** Let me check the workflow for `timeout-minutes:` at job level. Also check `runs-on` for build-macos — self-hosted runners: GitHub's default job timeout is 360 minutes; step timeouts work on self-hosted.

15. **The `if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]`** — hardcodes 4; consistent with `for attempt in 1 2 3 4`. If someone bumps to 5 in one place only, the last-atempt message misfires (prints "resuming in 5s..." then loop ends). Minor maintainability nit; the test's DownloadLoop.parse counts attempts and the worst-case check would catch budget drift but not this desync. Could suggest deriving from the list (`if [ "$attempt" = "${attempt}" ]`... no — better: use `${loop_last}`... in plain bash: compare against the last element or use a different loop). Actually simplest robust form: `for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do ... done` then after loop the failure message doesn't need attempt-specific branches at all — the current structure already handles it adequately. The desync risk is real but minor (SUGESTION).

      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework

          set -euo pipefail

          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"

  # Issue #280 AC3: nightly RELEASE-mode build matrix. The PR legs in
  # ci.yml build --debug (compile-truth); release-only concerns —
  # tree-shaking, R8/minify, dart2js optimisation, icon stripping — are

  # there officially yet, so they stay nightly-only per the card's
  # non-goals). A red leg feeds the deduped nightly-red issue via the
  # auto-issue job below.
  build-release:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} (release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build macos --release
          - target: ios
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build ios --release --no-codesign
          - target: android
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build apk --flavor store --release
          - target: web
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build web --release
      # The prebuilt WasmRun XCFramework is excluded from git; Apple builds
      # fail in the Podfile FFI-symbol check without it. Pinned upstream
      # release, same fallback as the ci.yml build legs.
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun framework (Apple targets)
        if: matrix.target == 'ios' || matrix.target == 'macos'
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/${{ matrix.target }}/Frameworks"
          rm -rf "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
            -o /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip \
            https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip
          unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      # The macOS Podfile bundles the LiteRT-LM companion dylibs via a
      # Runner script phase that fails on a fresh runner ("Could not find
      # macOS companion dylibs") — seed from the pinned upstream native
      # release, sha256-verified (same incantation as build-macos.yml).
      - name: Ensure flutter_gemma macOS companion dylibs
        if: matrix.target == 'macos'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GEMMA_CACHE="$HOME/Library/Caches/flutter_gemma/native/macos_arm64"

Now, let me consolidate my findings:

### Findings

**A. (IMPORTANT — SUGESTION?) `wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null` stderr leak + minor**: when $ZIP doesn't exist, the redirect error message still prints to the log (redirect processed before 2>/dev/null), and `tr -d '` strips only spaces, not tabs — wc's output has only spaces on macOS, fine. Actually simpler robust form: `got=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)` — wait that doesn't parse digits. Or `stat -f%z`. This is cosmetic. → SUGESTION.

**B. `if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]` hardcodes the attempt count** — desync risk if someone edits the loop list but not the literal. The gh-1149 history shows exactly this class of drift (off-by-one budget). The test pins `atempts >= 1` and the budget, but not the literal sync between the list and the `[ = "4" ]`. → SUGESTION (could be IMPORTANT? The failure mode if desynced: last-atempt message wrong (cosmetic — says "resuming in 5s" then loop ends, sleeps 5s extra... wait no: if loop list became 1..5 but the check stays =4: attempt 4 fails → message "out of loop attempts"... no wait, `if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]` prints "out of loop attempts" but then NO sleep, and attempt 5 runs immediately. And attempt 5 failing → no message at all, no sleep. Then got check. Budget-wise the test catches the cap overrun. The impact is purely message/no-sleep-before-last-atempt. Genuinely cosmetic → SUGESTION.)

**C. build-mobile.yml iOS WasmRun step unchanged — same bug class** (gh-1149 off-by-one: --retry 3 --max-time 600 → worst case 4×600=240s ≫ 900s step cap; no --fail; no digest pin; arch-less /tmp path; treadmill without -C -). Pre-existing, out of diff → general comment as IMPORTANT follow-up. Actually — is this scope creep to demand? No — flaging as follow-up in general comment is right. Also nightly.yml same curl shape but hosted runners (fast links, and nightly matrix timeout 45m job / step 15m — 240s worst > 900s step cap even there! Worst case only materializes with slow links; hosted = fast. But the arithmetic issue exists. I'll mention build-mobile as the main one since it's self-hosted (slow-link reality), nightly hosted in passing.)

**D. Cross-run/cross-job concurrent same-arch writers** — two overlapping build-macos runs (different refs — concurrency group is per-ref, cancel-in-progress: false; daily-publish leg + manual dispatch/tag build) on the same self-hosted runner → same `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-arm64.zip` → two curl -C - writers interleave → torn partial → digest gate purges → self-heals next run (both runs red that day). Pre-existing exposure (old rm -f interleaved too), not worsened materially; the per-run `rm -f` in the old code actually made cross-run overlap MORE destructive (unlink in-flight). New code: no unlink of in-flight (only purge after loop when THIS job's file is not in flight... wait — the purge `rm -f "$ZIP"` could delete the OTHER job's in-flight partial if the other job is mid-download with the same arch and same path! Scenario: runs A and B overlap, same arch. A is mid-atempt-3 downloading. B finishes its attempts (its curl failed early), got < ASET_BYTES → keep, exit 1 (no rm) — fine. OR B's got == ASET_BYTES && digest fail → B purges A's in-flight file! Then A's curl continues writing to the unlinked inode (POSIX: the file handle persists), A completes into the unlinked inode, A's wc -c reads the PATH → file gone → got=0 → keep branch → exit 1 (message "resumes from byte 0"). Next run: clean partial → works. So worst case: both overlapping runs fail; next daily run heals. No wedge. Acceptable. → SUGESTION: a `flock`/lockfile or `concurrency` note could tighten, but self-healing makes it non-blocking.)

**E. The purge branch can also fire when got == ASET_BYTES but digest fails due to A's CONCURRENT writes** — covered in D.

**F. Dead code / duplication in test file?** The test's DownloadLoop.parse etc. — fine. The `memory/note` — convention-consistent.

**G. Test britleness**: tests assert on exact message substrings ("keeping the partial", `rm -f "$ZIP"`, ASET_DIGEST=...) — established style in this repo for workflow lint tests (string-lint style). Acceptable. The `run.lastIndexOf('shasum -a 256 -c -')` — fine.

**H. Any issue with `restoreStep()` requiring exactly one step with that name** — build-mobile has "Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework" (different name) — no collision. ✓

**I. Verify the claim "macOS prunes only 3-day-untouched /tmp files"** — accurate for macOS daily periodic cleanup.

**J. One more potential BLOCKING check — the post-loop digest check failing when the download SUCCEEDED via break**: `if [ "$got" -eq "$ASET_BYTES" ] && echo ... shasum -c; then : ; elif ...` — if break happened and digest fails (corupt upstream/impossible for immutable asset — or INTERLEAVED writes from overlapping runs, case D): got == ASET_BYTES → elif false → else → purge → exit 1. Correct.

And the elif ordering: `[ "$got" -eq "$ASET_BYTES" ] && shasum` — if sizes match but digest fails → the whole && chain is false → elif got < ASET_BYTES? No (equal) → else purge. ✓. If sizes DON'T match (less) → elif → keep+exit. If greater → else purge. ✓ All paths correct.

**K. `unzip -q "$ZIP"` after the skip path uses the pre-loop-validated zip — validated ✓.

**L. Is `shasum` guaranteed on macOS runners? Yes (macOS ships shasum; the litertlm step already relies on it).

**M. x86_64 leg: LOCAL_SRC branch — `cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"` — if BOTH arch jobs run and one is in `cp -R` while the other unzips into the same DEST → pre-existing.

**N. Comment accuracy**: "29.5MB (x86_64) / 73% (arm64)" — ticket log shows arm64 25818587/5170304 — wait, that's odd: 5170304 out of... the log says "with 25818587 out of 5170304 bytes received" — that's 25.8MB of 51.77MB = 49.9%. Hmm! The log excerpt in the ticket shows curl (28) after 239708ms with 25818587 out of 5170304 bytes. But the asset is 97,238,501 bytes. Why does curl say 5170304 total? Because -C - resume: the "out of 5170304" is the REMAING range (97,238,501 − 45,468,197 = 51,70,304). So arm64 had banked 45,468,197 bytes (46.7%) from prior attempts, and this final attempt got 25.8MB more of the remaining 51.77MB → total banked ≈ 71.3MB = 73%. ✓ The PR's "73% (arm64)" matches the log evidence (and the test comment cites `Resuming transfer from byte position 45468197` — consistent: 45,468,197 + 25,818,587 = 71,286,784 = 73.3% of 97,238,501 ✓). The numbers are internally consistent. Nice.

x86_64 "29.5MB": 3 × 240s at ~40KB/s ≈ 28.8MB ≈ 29.5MB plausible ✓.

403:       - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
404:         timeout-minutes: 20
405:         run: |
406:           set -euo pipefail
407:           # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
408:           # 1) actions/cache hit (keyed by the release tag) — warm until the
409:           #    repo's daily cache churn LRU-evicts the entry (saved 10-20
410:           #    06:02Z, gone by 10-21 19:03Z: gh-1759 ran cold twice);
411:           # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
412:           # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the step
413:           #    cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): retries live in THIS
414:           #    bash loop, not curl --retry (which adds N MORE attempts AND
415:           #    restarts+truncates instead of resuming). Worst case with the
416:           #    gh-1759 budget: 4 × 240s max-time + 3 × 5s sleeps = 975s,
417:           #    + connect + unzip + slack ≈ 1035s < the 20-min (1200s) cap.
418:           #
419:           #    gh-1759: the gh-1149 budget (3 × 240s) was sized for this
420:           #    link's good-day ~300KB/s. The 10-21 daily run measured
421:           #    40–108KB/s (cold cache, both arch jobs): 3 × 240s banked
422:           #    only 29.5MB (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) of the 97,238,501-byte
423:           #    asset and the leg went red. Resume worked (`Resuming
424:           #    transfer from byte position …` in the logs) — the wire
425:           #    budget was simply too small, and the old pre-loop wipe
426:           #    threw each run's partial away, so a slow-link day never
427:           #    banked durable progress and the leg could not self-heal.
428:           #    Fixes: (a) the per-arch /tmp partial now PERSISTS across
429:           #    runs — -C - resumes it within the step AND across daily
430:           #    runs (macOS prunes only 3-day-untouched /tmp files; a daily
431:           #    run touches it) until the asset completes and the
432:           #    actions/cache post-step saves the framework; (b) the loop
433:           #    grew to 4 × 240s under a 20-min step cap.
434:           LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
435:           DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
436:           # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
437:           # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
438:           # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
439:           # let one job's cleanup unlink the other's in-flight partial,
440:           # then both curls interleave bytes into one path.
441:           ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
442:           # The release asset is immutable per tag — pin its digest so a
443:           # wrong-content-but-valid-zip cannot slip past unzip CRC32 into
444:           # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache (same pattern
445:           # as the litertlm download above). The pinned byte size tells a
446:           # truncated download (KEEP the partial — the next run resumes
447:           # it) apart from a complete-but-wrong one (PURGE and restart).
448:           ASSET_DIGEST="aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98"
449:           ASSET_BYTES=97238501
450:           mkdir -p "$DEST"
451:           if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
452:             echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
453:           elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
454:             echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
455:             cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
456:           else
457:             echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
458:             # The partial is deliberately NOT deleted between runs
459:             # (gh-1759): it is exactly what -C - is for. If the persisted
460:             # zip is already complete AND digest-valid, skip the download
461:             # — a -C - attempt against a complete file gets HTTP 416 and
462:             # reads success as failure.
463:             if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
464:               echo "Complete, digest-valid $ZIP persisted from an earlier run — skipping download"
465:             else
466:               for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
467:                 # --fail: without it curl exits 0 on HTTP 404/5xx and writes
468:                 # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error
469:                 # engages this loop's retries. -C - makes each attempt
470:                 # RESUME the partial zip (Range requests), so slow links
471:                 # make forward progress within this step AND across runs.
472:                 if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
473:                   -o "$ZIP" \
474:                   https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
475:                   break
476:                 fi
477:                 if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]; then
478:                   echo "download attempt $attempt failed — out of loop attempts" >&2
479:                 else
480:                   echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
481:                   sleep 5
482:                 fi
483:               done
484:               got=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || echo 0)
485:               if [ "$got" -eq "$ASSET_BYTES" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -; then
486:                 : # complete and authentic — fall through to unzip
487:               elif [ "$got" -lt "$ASSET_BYTES" ]; then
488:                 echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip incomplete: $got / $ASSET_BYTES bytes after $attempt attempts — keeping the partial; the next run resumes from byte $got (gh-1759)" >&2
489:                 exit 1
490:               else
491:                 echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip is $got bytes (expected $ASSET_BYTES) or failed its pinned sha256 — purging it so the next run restarts clean" >&2
492:                 rm -f "$ZIP"
493:                 exit 1
494:               fi
495:             fi
496:             unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
497:           fi
498:           ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
499:

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1775
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1775
- **Title**: gh-1759 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1759` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +211
- **Deletions**: -80
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:57:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T23:47:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1759
### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. Resume itself worked (`Resuming transfer from byte position …` in the logs), but the pre-loop `rm -f "$ZIP"` discarded each run's partial, so no daily run ever banked durable progress. The cache fallback was cold too: the `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` entry saved 10-20 06:02Z was LRU-evicted by the repo's daily cache churn before 10-21 19:03Z (both jobs logged `Cache not found`).

### Previous Attempt
gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.
- ci.yml / nightly.yml WasmRun steps run on GitHub-hosted runners (600s attempts, datacenter links) — intentionally unchanged.

```bash

...
ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${ matrix.arch }}.zip"
ASET_DIGEST="aca903d73202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98"

mkdir -p "$DEST"
if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
 echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then

else

 if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$ASET_DIGEST $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   echo "Complete, digest-valid $ZIP persisted from an earlier run — skipping download"
 else
   for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
     if curl --fail -L -C --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
       -o "$ZIP" \
       https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
       break
     fi

       echo "download attempt $attempt failed — out of loop attempts" >&2
     else
       echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
       sleep 5
     fi
   done
   got=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' || echo 0)
   if [ "$got" -eq "$ASET_BYTES" ] && echo "$ASET_DIGEST $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -; then
     : # complete and authentic — fall through to unzip
   elif [ "$got" -lt "$ASET_BYTES" ]; then
     echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip incomplete: $got / $ASET_BYTES bytes after $attempt attempts — keeping the partial; the next run resumes from byte $got (gh-1759)" >&2
     exit 1
   else
     echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip is $got bytes (expected $ASET_BYTES) or failed its pinned sha256 — purging it so the next run restarts clean" >&2

     exit 1
   fi

Potential issues I've identified so far:

1. **Pre-loop digest gate vs. incomplete partial**: If the persisted partial is INCOMPLETE (e.g., 30MB of 97MB), the pre-loop gate's shasum fails (of course) → enters loop → curl -C - resumes from 30MB. Good — the gate only skips on complete+valid.

2. **`wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null`** — if $ZIP doesn't exist (all attempts failed before creating the file), bash prints an error to stderr (the redirect error isn't suppressed because `< "$ZIP"` is processed before `2>/dev/null`), but the `|| echo 0` handles the pipeline failure. Cosmetic log noise; behavior correct (got=0 → incomplete branch → keep → exit 1). Very minor.

Wait, actually — one more check: does curl with `--fail` on a 404 create the output file? Modern curl: `-o` file is created/opened when the transfer starts... Actually with `--fail`, since curl 7.76? No — let me think. There's a curl behavior: "--fail ... fail silently (no output at all) on server errors" and importantly, since curl 7.75.0? Hmm, there was a change: "curl --fail no longer writes the error body". And regarding file creation: curl creates the output file lazily on first write? No — curl creates/truncates the output file BEFORE sending the request, historically. Actually, I recall `curl -o out http://404` leaves a 0-byte out file. Yes, curl creates the output file early. So a 404 with --fail typically leaves a 0-byte $ZIP. Either way (file exists 0 bytes, or doesn't exist), got=0 → keep branch → exit 1. Correct.

3. **The success check `if [ "$got" -eq "$ASET_BYTES" ] && echo ... | shasum -a 256 -c -; then`** — note shasum here does NOT suppress stderr/stdout — on success it prints "$ZIP: OK" to stdout. Good for logs.

4. **`[ "$got" -lt "$ASET_BYTES" ]` keep branch when $ZIP missing entirely** — got=0 → keep → exit 1 with message "resumes from byte 0". Fine.

5. **Oversize partial (got > ASET_BYTES) with VALID digest impossible** — fine.

6. **The one hole: complete-size partial (got == ASET_BYTES) with WRONG digest → purge branch.** But note: the pre-loop gate would ALSO have failed for this zip, so the loop runs, 4 × 416-failures (fast), then purge. OK.

7. **NOW — the interesting one: what if `curl` succeeds on attempt N (break) but the file is INCOMPLETE?** As analyzed, curl exit 0 with -C - means the full remaining range was received. But consider: GitHub redirects `-L` to S3/objects.githubusercontent.com — if the redirect target serves the FULL file ignoring the Range header... with `-C -`, curl first makes a HEAD-ish? No: with `-C -`, curl asks the server for the range; the server (S3) honors Range. If a server ignores Range and returns 200 full-content while resuming, curl errors with 33 ("HTTP server doesn't seem to support byte ranges"). Hmm, is that exactly right? curl with `-C -` receiving a 200 instead of 206: it aborts with error 33. Yes.

  BUT the subtle one: what if the response is 206 but with a SHORT body and clean TLS close → curl exit 18 (partial file) → treated as failure → retry. Fine.

8. **`set -e` interaction with `if curl ...; then break; fi`** — curl failure inside if-condition is fine.

9. **The `attempt` variable after loop when the loop is skipped**: If the pre-loop gate succeeds (skip download), the `for` loop never runs, `unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"` runs — $ZIP is the complete valid zip. Good.

10. **`unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"` — unzip into shared DEST while the OTHER arch job might be doing the same** — pre-existing shared-DEST race, content identical. Not new. I might mention as a general observation, pre-existing.

11. **The 20-min timeout vs. the workflow's job-level timeout** — need to check if job-level timeout-minutes exists that's < 20. Let me check.

12. **`ASET_BYTES`/`ASET_DIGEST` hardcoded per asset URL** — if the URL is ever bumped, the digest must be updated; the test pins the digest value so drift is caught. Good.

13. **Comment math**: "Worst case with the gh-1759 budget: 4 × 240s max-time + 3 × 5s sleeps = 975s, + connect + unzip + slack ≈ 1035s < the 20-min (120s) cap." — connect-timeout is inside --max-time, so 4 × 240 already covers connect. The +60s reserve covers shasum (twice: pre-loop gate + post-loop check — each ~97MB hash) + wc + unzip + ls. shasum -a 256 on a 97MB file: Digest::SHA via Perl is roughly 100-250MB/s on Apple Silicon → <1s each. unzip -q of a 92.7MB zip → few seconds. OK, reserve is adequate.

14. **`timeout-minutes: 20` — but is there a job-level timeout?** Let me check the workflow for `timeout-minutes:` at job level. Also check `runs-on` for build-macos — self-hosted runners: GitHub's default job timeout is 360 minutes; step timeouts work on self-hosted.

15. **The `if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]`** — hardcodes 4; consistent with `for attempt in 1 2 3 4`. If someone bumps to 5 in one place only, the last-atempt message misfires (prints "resuming in 5s..." then loop ends). Minor maintainability nit; the test's DownloadLoop.parse counts attempts and the worst-case check would catch budget drift but not this desync. Could suggest deriving from the list (`if [ "$attempt" = "${attempt}" ]`... no — better: use `${loop_last}`... in plain bash: compare against the last element or use a different loop). Actually simplest robust form: `for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do ... done` then after loop the failure message doesn't need attempt-specific branches at all — the current structure already handles it adequately. The desync risk is real but minor (SUGESTION).

16. **GitHub Actions `${ matrix.arch }}` inside the run block** — expression interpolation, safe (workflow-controlled). Pre-existing pattern.

17. **Security review of the persistence change**: The persisted partial in /tmp on a SELF-HOSTED runner — /tmp is world-writable. A malicious local process could pre-place a zip at `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-arm64.zip` that is complete + digest-valid... but then it's the authentic asset (sha256 preimage). A WRONG-content zip would fail the digest gate and be re-downloaded/purged. TOCTOU between the gate …

      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

  # Issue #280 AC3: nightly RELEASE-mode build matrix. The PR legs in
  # ci.yml build --debug (compile-truth); release-only concerns —
  # tree-shaking, R8/minify, dart2js optimisation, icon stripping — are
  # verified here, plus linux/windows bonus targets (the app does not ship
  # there officially yet, so they stay nightly-only per the card's
  # non-goals). A red leg feeds the deduped nightly-red issue via the
  # auto-issue job below.
  build-release:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} (release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build macos --release
          - target: ios
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build ios --release --no-codesign
          - target: android
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build apk --flavor store --release
          - target: web
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build web --release
      # The prebuilt WasmRun XCFramework is excluded from git; Apple builds
      # fail in the Podfile FFI-symbol check without it. Pinned upstream
      # release, same fallback as the ci.yml build legs.
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun framework (Apple targets)
        if: matrix.target == 'ios' || matrix.target == 'macos'
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/${{ matrix.target }}/Frameworks"
          rm -rf "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
            -o /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip \
            https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip
          unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      # The macOS Podfile bundles the LiteRT-LM companion dylibs via a
      # Runner script phase that fails on a fresh runner ("Could not find
      # macOS companion dylibs") — seed from the pinned upstream native
      # release, sha256-verified (same incantation as build-macos.yml).
      - name: Ensure flutter_gemma macOS companion dylibs
        if: matrix.target == 'macos'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GEMMA_CACHE="$HOME/Library/Caches/flutter_gemma/native/macos_arm64"
